ai.description: This slender snake reaches 70–90 cm. It is dark brown or black with thin, pale crossbands and a white upper lip. Key features include a flattened head and enlarged, fang-like teeth in the upper jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Lycodon septentrionalis* by the presence of a distinct, broad white or yellow collar on the nape, which is absent in most other similar Indian wolf snakes.
ai.habitat: *Lycodon septentrionalis* inhabits humid, forested regions of the Himalayan foothills and Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Northern Large-toothed Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for prey such as geckos and small skinks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon septentrionalis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–8 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing by late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon septentrionalis* occurs in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Nagaland) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically ranging from 200 to 2,000 meters in elevation.
